comments.note: UpdateDiffState() calls SetProperty (via HasDifferences = ... and ScrollTargetIndex = ...) then OnPropertyChanged(string.Empty). HasDifferences will receive two PropertyChanged notifications per UpdateDiffState() call — one from SetProperty and one from the bulk string.Empty broadcast. This is harmless (WPF bindings are idempotent) and is documented CommunityToolkit.Mvvm behavior, but worth noting as a minor redundancy.

OnPropertyChanged(string.Empty) correctly broadcasts refreshes for all computed properties including ones not previously listed (e.g., ShowMovedGuidance, HasRemovedMods, count text strings). The change is strictly broader than the 24-call approach and eliminates any risk of missing a newly-added computed property.

comments.note: UpdateDiffState() is now a clean, maintainable 3-line method: HasDifferences assignment, ScrollTargetIndex assignment, then OnPropertyChanged(string.Empty). The structure is straightforwardly readable and aligns perfectly with the CommunityToolkit.Mvvm documented convention. No long-term maintenance concerns — new computed properties added to this ViewModel will be automatically covered by the bulk notification without any developer action.

Double-notification on HasDifferences (confirmed by QA): SetProperty raises PropertyChanged for 'HasDifferences', then OnPropertyChanged(string.Empty) raises it again for all properties. WPF data binding is idempotent so there is no behavioral issue, and this is an accepted trade-off of the bulk-refresh pattern in CommunityToolkit.Mvvm. If micro-optimization ever becomes necessary, the two SetProperty calls could be refactored to set the backing fields directly (_hasDifferences, _scrollTargetIndex) before calling OnPropertyChanged(string.Empty) once — but this would be premature at current scale.

The GuidanceVisibility_UpdatesAfterDiffRefresh test is well-structured: it captures the PropertyChanged event, mutates the collection, verifies both the behavioral assertion (visibility flips) and the notification assertion (string.Empty fired). The comment on line 331 accurately explains the semantic of string.Empty, which is good for future maintainers reading the test.

[documentation-forward] UpdateDiffState() now uses OnPropertyChanged(string.Empty) as a bulk refresh, but the method has no XML doc comment. A brief <summary> explaining that it recomputes HasDifferences, ScrollTargetIndex, and triggers a full property-change broadcast would help future contributors understand why string.Empty is used here rather than specific nameof() calls, and distinguish it from the targeted OnPropertyChanged calls used in OnMainViewModelPropertyChanged and OnIsConfigValidChanged.

[documentation-forward] The GuidanceVisibility_UpdatesAfterDiffRefresh test's inline comment ('string.Empty signals all properties changed') is helpful but brief. A one-sentence reference to the CommunityToolkit.Mvvm convention (e.g. 'per CommunityToolkit.Mvvm convention, PropertyChanged with string.Empty/null signals a full refresh of all properties') would improve discoverability for contributors unfamiliar with the convention.
